title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'equation of loops' in the profinite Teichmüller tower in genus 1. The objects are the order-6 and order-4 elements rho, sigma (images of the standard torsion of SL2(Z)), and the groups G_{rho,sigma}, Gamma_{rho,sigma} and Z_rho. Gamma_Q^~ is his candidate 'Teichmüller' group, the later GT-hat, which contains Gamma_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q). tau_gamma is complex conjugation, an involution. To each u in M'[0] are attached signs eps_2, eps_3 with eps_3 = (-1)^{nu_3}, elements alpha, beta of Pi^hat, and a 'correction' a = alpha^{-1} u in Z_rho. From (43)-(43ter), delta(u) = tau_gamma^{nu_3} delta(a), where delta is the map to Gamma_Q^~. The previous page showed that beta'' = u'(beta) beta' and that eps'' = eps' eps. The open question is whether u -> a is multiplicative: a'' = a'a, which implies (*) delta(a'') = delta(a') delta(a).

The computation on this page.
- Compare delta(u'u) = tau^{nu_3+nu'_3} delta(a'') with delta(u') delta(u) = tau^{nu'_3} delta(a') tau^{nu_3} delta(a).
- Cancel the left factor tau^{nu'_3} and use tau^2 = 1. This gives (47): delta(a'') = int(tau^{nu_3})(delta(a')) · delta(a).
- Hence (*) is equivalent to (48): [delta(a'), tau^{nu_3}] = 1. Since delta(u') differs from delta(a') by a power of tau, this is the same as [delta(u'), tau^{nu_3}] = 1.
- So if nu_3 = 0 (eps_3 = +1), multiplicativity is automatic.
- If eps_3 = -1, it forces delta(u') to commute with complex conjugation. Grothendieck calls this 'draconian'.

Conjecture and conclusion.
- For an element of Gamma_Q this should force u' to lie in {1, tau_gamma}: in Gal(Qbar/Q) complex conjugation is self-centralizing.
- He states heuristically that the same should hold for every element of Gamma_Q^~. In modern terms: the centralizer of complex conjugation in GT-hat is {1, tau}.
- Consequently the success of the presentation of §48 (chapter XI) rested on special situations where the groups Gamma_{rho,sigma} ≃ Zhat^* are commutative, so that tau_gamma is central.
- In general, a = alpha^{-1} u depends multiplicatively on u only when one restricts to u in the index-2 subgroup M'[0]' (eps_3 = +1).
- The next page goes on to parametrize the lifts (u,a,b) of a fixed u explicitly via alpha rho^j eps_3(tau') and beta sigma^i.
errors: Minor: in the intermediate line he writes tau^{nu_3} on both sides and then strikes it out. The correct manipulation is left-multiplication by tau^{-nu'_3}, followed by tau^{-nu_3} = tau^{nu_3} (tau is an involution). The final formula (47) and the equivalence (48) are correct.

The claim that commutation with tau forces u' in {1, tau} for all of Gamma_Q^~ is explicitly heuristic, not proved. For Gamma_Q it follows from Artin–Schreier type arguments: complex conjugations in G_Q are self-centralizing.

ideas.what: Reduction of the multiplicativity (cocycle) condition for the correction term a(u) to commutation of delta(u') with complex conjugation when eps_3 = -1
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle/twisting computation for a section of an extension by an involution

ideas.what: Self-centralizing property of complex conjugation in Gal(Qbar/Q)
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer of an involution in the absolute Galois group (Artin–Schreier)

ideas.what: Heuristic conjecture that the centralizer of complex conjugation in Gamma_Q^~ (GT-hat) is {1, tau}
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer of complex conjugation in the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; torsion and involutions in GT-hat were studied by Lochak–Schneps and others in the 1990s

ideas.what: Diagnosis that an earlier presentation (§48, ch. XI) worked only because tau is central in Gamma_{rho,sigma} ≃ Zhat^*, and that multiplicativity holds on the index-2 subgroup eps_3 = +1
ideas.modern_name: Restriction to the orientation/sign-preserving subgroup for a well-defined homomorphism

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures, heuristically, that the only elements of the Teichmüller/GT-type group Gamma_Q^~ commuting with complex conjugation are 1 and tau, i.e. that complex conjugation is self-centralizing in GT-hat as it is in Gal(Qbar/Q).
missed.quote: C'est une condition draconienne sur un élément de Γ_Q^~ qui, pour un élément de Γ_Q lui-même devrait impliquer que u'∈{1,τ_γ} — et par des arguments heuristiques, on sent qu'il devrait en être ainsi pour tout élément de Γ_Q^~.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT-hat shares this Galois-theoretic property of G_Q is a natural test of the conjecture GT-hat = G_Q (or of the differences between them). I am unsure whether the centralizer of complex conjugation in GT-hat has been determined. If not, this is an open, concrete question dating back to Grothendieck.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is routine. It does contain an explicit unpublished heuristic conjecture: complex conjugation is self-centralizing in GT-hat. This is a natural and specific statement, but similar questions (torsion and involutions in GT-hat) were studied later, and its novelty is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: Left margin: should read 'puisque δ(u) = τ_γ^{ν_3} δ(a)', not 'δ(a) = τ_γ^{ν_3}δ(a)'.
'a = a'^{-1}u ∈ Z_p ↪ G_{p,σ}' should be 'a = α^{-1}u ∈ Z_ρ ↪ G_{ρ,σ}'. The subscripts are ρ, not p, throughout, so Γ_{p,σ} should be Γ_{ρ,σ}.
'condition de 2e bonne : dans u∈M'[0]'' likely reads 'à condition de se borner aux u ∈ M'[0]''.
'tient en fait qu'en dans la situation' likely reads 'tient en fait à ce que dans les situations [traitées]...'.
Insertion above the line: 'où τ_γ central' (τ_γ is central in Γ_{ρ,σ}).
The crossed bottom-left margin seems to say that τ_γ should be central in Γ_{ρ,σ} = Ker(...).
